CLAREMONT CITY COUNCIL
  MEETING AGENDA
  “We are a vibrant, livable, and inclusive community dedicated to quality services,
  safety, financial strength, sustainability, preservation, and progress
  with equal representation for our community.”

City Council Chamber  Tuesday
225 Second Street  June 22, 2021
Claremont, CA 91711
  6:30 PM

  COUNCILMEMBERS

  JENNIFER STARK
  MAYOR

  COREY CALAYCAY  JED LEANO  SAL MEDINA  ED REECE

Pursuant to the local emergency concerning the COVID-19 virus declared by
the City Council of the City of Claremont on March 19, 2020, the Los Angeles
County Department of Health's "Safer at Home Order" issued March 19, 2020,
and Executive Order N-29-20 issued by Governor Gavin Newsom on March
18, 2020, the following protocols will apply to public participation for the
duration of the emergency:

Members of the public will not be permitted to be physically present at meetings. To allow for public
participation, the City Council will conduct its meeting through Zoom Video Communications. To
participate in the meeting from the comfort of your own home or office, download Zoom on any phone or
computer device and copy and paste the following link into your browser to access and participate in the
live City Council meeting at 6:30 p.m.: https://zoom.us/j/256208090 or to only listen from the phone dial
(213)338-8477,  Webinar  ID:  256 208 090.  For  assistance,  please  call  (909)399-5461 or
(909)399-5463.

Members of the public who wish to address the City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or a
subject matter within the jurisdiction of the City Council may utilize the following methods. The Council
requests, but does not require, the public speakers to identify themselves.

OPTION 1: LIVE COMMENTS - Through Zoom, someone wishing to speak may virtually "raise your
hand". Wait to be called upon by the City Clerk, and then you may provide verbal comments for up to 4
minutes.

OPTION 2: E-MAIL - Public comments may be sent via email to the City Clerk’s office at
sdesautels@ci.claremont.ca.us or jcostanza@ci.claremont.ca.us. All emails received before 3:00 p.m.,
will be distributed to the City Council, imaged into the City’s document archive system, and read into the
record (up to 4 minutes).
 Page 2  City Council Agenda  June 22, 2021

OPTION 3: MAIL - Public comments may be mailed to Claremont City Hall, Attn: City Clerk’s Office, PO
Box 880, Claremont, CA 91711. All comments received via mail will be distributed to the City Council,
imaged into the City’s document archive system, and read into the record (up to 4 minutes).

OPTION 4: TELEPHONICALLY - Members of the public wanting to address the City Council
telephonically are requested to inform the Claremont City Clerk's office no later than 3:00 p.m. on the
day of the meeting.  The Claremont City Clerk's office can be reached at (909) 399-5461, (909)
399-5463, sdesautels@ci.claremont.ca.us, or jcostanza@ci.claremont.ca.us. You will be called during
consideration of the item you are interested in and given up to 4 minutes to speak.

The meeting will not be live streamed through Granicus as the meeting will be live streamed through
Zoom instead. The recorded meeting will be uploaded and saved as a record.

CALL TO ORDER THE MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MOMENT OF SILENCE

ROLL CALL

  Outstanding Academic Achievement - Seniors from Claremont High School and San

  Akshay Patel, Sebastian Ramos, Therese Reisch, Kamran Sheriff, Ethan Villegas, and
  Charles Warren

MAYOR AND COUNCIL

Council Items

Council Assignment Reports
City Councilmembers may serve as representatives on regional organizations. This time is
allocated for reports about their activities. For information about the Council's local,
intergovernmental  and  regional  appointments  please  visit  the  City  website :
https://www.ci.claremont.ca.us/government/city-council/city-council-assignments-and-appointment
s.

CITY MANAGER REPORT
 Page 3  City Council Agenda  June 22, 2021

PUBLIC COMMENT
The Council has set aside this time for persons in the audience who wish to comment on items
that ARE NOT LISTED ON THIS AGENDA, but are within the jurisdiction of the City Council.
Members of the audience will later have the opportunity to address the City Council regarding ALL
OTHER ITEMS ON THE AGENDA at the time the Council considers those items.

At this time the Council will take public comment for 30 minutes. Public Comment will resume later
in the meeting if there are speakers who did not get an opportunity to speak because of the
30-minute time limit.

The Brown Act prohibits the City Council from taking action on oral requests relating to items that
are not on the agenda. The Council may engage in a brief discussion, refer the matter to staff,
and/or schedule requests for consideration at a subsequent meeting.

The Council requests, but does not require, speakers to identify themselves. When you come up
to speak, please state your name unless you wish to remain anonymous. Each speaker will be
allowed four (4) continuous minutes.

CONSENT CALENDAR
All matters listed on the consent calendar are considered to be routine. The City Council or one or
more Commissions and/or Committees have previously considered most of the items on the
consent calendar. The Council may act on these items by one motion following public comment.

Only Councilmembers may pull an item from the consent calendar for discussion.

The City Council will waive reading of resolutions and ordinances. Each resolution and ordinance
will be numbered following Council approval.

Now is the time for those in the audience to comment on the consent calendar. Each speaker will
be allowed four (4) continuous minutes to comment on items on the consent calendar.
1.  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION APPROVING THE CITY WARRANT REGISTER
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, ALLOWING
  CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT
  OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID, dated June 10, 2021.
  Attachment(s):  Resolution Approving City Warrant Register Dated June 10, 2021

2.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 8, 2021 (SPECIAL AND REGULAR)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council approve and file the special and
  regular City Council meeting minutes of June 8, 2021.
  Attachment(s):  Draft Special Meeting Minutes of June 8, 2021
  Draft Regular Meeting Minutes of June 8, 2021
 Page 4  City Council Agenda  June 22, 2021

3.  FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATING AGREEMENT WITH VILLAGE
  PARTNERS VENTURES, LLC FOR THE POTENTIAL PURCHASE OF CITY-OWNED
  PROPERTY, LOCATED AT 451 WEST ARROW HIGHWAY (FUNDING SOURCE: GENERAL
  FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to
  execute a First Amendment to the Exclusive Negotiating Agreement with
  Village Partners Ventures, LLC., to extend the negotiating period for the
  potential purchase of City-owned property located at 451 West Arrow
  Highway.
4.  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENTS WITH
  KEYSER MARSTON ASSOCIATES, INC. AND NEIGHBORHOOD PARTNERSHIP HOUSING
  SERVICES, INC. FOR INCLUSIONARY HOUSING SERVICES (FUNDING SOURCE:
  INCLUSIONARY HOUSING DEPOSITS)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  A. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a professional services
  agreement with Keyser Marston Associates, Inc., effective July 1, 2021, with
  a compensation cap of $50,000 per year for three years; and
  B. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a professional services
  agreement with Neighborhood Housing Partnership Services, Inc., effective
  July 1, 2021, with a compensation cap of $50,000 per year for three-years.
5.  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO A MEASURE M AGREEMENT FOR BICYCLE AND
  PEDESTRIAN IMPROVEMENTS AT COLLEGE AVENUE AND GREEN STREET AND
  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  ADVANTEC CONSULTING ENGINEERS FOR PROJECT ENGINEERING SERVICES
  (FUNDING SOURCE: MEASURE M FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that City Council:
  A. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Measure M Funding Agreement
  (FA#9200000000MM470303) between the Los Angeles County Metropolitan
  Transportation Authority and the City of Claremont; and
  B. Authorize the City Manager to execute a professional services agreement
  with Advantec Consulting Engineers in the amount of $79,440 to provide
  engineered plans and specifications for the project.
  Attachment(s):  Funding Agreement
  Excerpt from the 4/22/21 TTC Meeting Minutes

6.  A RESOLUTION ADOPTING A LIST OF SB1-FUNDED PROJECTS FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2021-22 (FUNDING SOURCE: STATE GAS TAX FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING A
  LIST OF PROJECTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021-22 FUNDED BY SB 1: THE
  ROAD REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017.
  Attachment(s):  SB1 Resolution 21-22
 Page 5  City Council Agenda  June 22, 2021

7.  AWARD OF CONTRACT TO SUPERIOR PAVEMENT MARKINGS, INC. FOR THE STREET
  STRIPING IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (FUNDING SOURCE: STATE GAS TAX FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  A. Authorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement with Superior
  Pavement Markings, Inc. for the 2020-21 CIP Street Striping Project
  (Harrison Avenue from Indian Hill Boulevard to Harvard Avenue, Cambridge
  Avenue from Arrow Highway to Bonita Avenue, First Street from Cornell
  Avenue to Indian Hill Boulevard, the intersection of Base Line Road and
  Monte Vista Avenue, Monte Vista Avenue from Base Line Road to the
  southern City limit, and Claremont Boulevard) in an amount not to exceed
  $105,536;
  B. Authorize a project contingency in the amount of $4,464;
  C. Authorize an amount not to exceed $10,000 for Extra Work as determined
  by the City; and
  D. Appropriate $20,000 from the State Gas Tax Fund to fully fund the project.
8.  AWARD OF CONTRACT TO ELECNOR BELCO ELECTRIC, INC., FOR THE CITYWIDE
  TRAFFIC SIGNAL IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT, CIP 2021-03 (FUNDING SOURCES:
  MEASURE M AND GAS TAX)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  A. Award a contract to Elecnor Belco Electric, Inc. for the Citywide Traffic
  Signal Improvements Project; and
  B. Authorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement with Elecnor Belco
  Electric, Inc. of Chino, in the amount of $479,153, and authorize a ten
  percent contingency in the amount of $47,915, for a total project cost of
  $527,068.
  Attachment(s):  Excerpt from the 3/25/21 TTC Meeting Minutes

9.  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH ECONOLITE SYSTEMS, INC.,
  FOR TRAFFIC SIGNAL MAINTENANCE SERVICES (FUNDING SOURCE: GENERAL FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a one-year agreement with Econolite Systems, Inc., for annual traffic
  signal maintenance in the amount of $125,000, with the option to extend the
  agreement for four additional one-year terms in an amount not to exceed
  $125,000 per year.
10. AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH DIAMOND ENVIRONMENTAL
  SERVICES TO PROVIDE PORTABLE RESTROOM SERVICES FOR THE CLAREMONT
  HILLS WILDERNESS PARK (FUNDING SOURCE: WILDERNESS PARK PARKING LOT
  FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into an agreement for one year with Diamond Environmental Services for an
  amount not to exceed $28,556.36 in the first year, with the option to extend
  the agreement for two additional one-year terms with a 4.7 percent increase
  each year.
 Page 6  City Council Agenda  June 22, 2021

11. AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  BLAIS & ASSOCIATES FOR GRANT RESEARCH AND MANAGEMENT SERVICES
  (FUNDING SOURCE: GENERAL FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a one-year professional services agreement with Blais & Associates in
  the amount of $25,000, with two optional one-year extensions in the amount
  of $25,000 per year.
12. AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  SILVER & WRIGHT LLP FOR SPECIAL LEGAL SERVICES RELATED TO CODE
  ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS (FUNDING SOURCE: GENERAL FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a one-year professional services agreement with Silver & Wright LLP in
  the amount of $60,000, with two optional one-year extensions in the amount
  of $60,000 per year.
13. AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH NCX GROUP TO PROVIDE
  NETWORK SECURITY MONITORING SERVICES (FUNDING SOURCE: GENERAL FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a new three-year agreement with NCX Group for network security
  monitoring services for an annual cost of $60,200 for 2021-22, $63,210 for
  2022-23, and $63,370 for 2023-24, with total compensation not to exceed
  $186,780 over the three-year term of the agreement.
14. 2021-22 PULSIAM (FORMERLY HITECH) MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT FOR COMPUTER
  AIDED  DISPATCH,  RECORDS  MANAGEMENT  SYSTEM,  AND MOBILE DATA
  COMMUNICATIONS SOFTWARE (FUNDING SOURCE: GENERAL FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that City Council authorize the City Manager to enter into
  a one-year agreement in the amount of $82,014.58 for 2021-22 to continue
  the existing maintenance contract with Pulsiam for Computer Aided Dispatch,
  Records Management System, and Mobile Data Communications software.
15. AWARD OF CONTRACT  FOR  PROFESSIONAL  AUDITING  SERVICES  (FUNDING
  SOURCE: GENERAL FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute a
  five-year agreement with Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP in the
  amount of $232,880 for professional auditing services.
 Page 7  City Council Agenda  June 22, 2021

16. RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE EXAMINATION OF SALES OR TRANSACTIONS AND
  USE TAX RECORDS AND AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO A PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH HINDERLITER DE LLAMAS & ASSOCIATES (HDL) FOR
  SALES & USE TAX DATA ANALYSIS AND CONSULTING SERVICES (FUNDING SOURCE:
  GENERAL FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  A. Adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING EXAMINATION OF SALES OR
  TRANSACTIONS AND USE TAX RECORDS; and
  B. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a professional services
  agreement with Hinderliter De Llamas & Associates (HDL) for Bradley-Burns
  sales and use tax data analysis and consulting services.
  Attachment(s):  Resolution

PUBLIC HEARINGS
Public Hearings will not begin before 7:00 p.m. Each speaker providing public comment will be
allowed four (4) continuous minutes to speak, which cannot be delegated.
17. ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION APPROVING THE REVISED DELINQUENT SANITATION
  ACCOUNT REPORT OF JUNE 22, 2021 AND ORDERING THE PLACEMENT OF LIENS
  UPON REAL PROPERTY FOR THE UNPAID SANITATION AND SEWER MAINTENANCE
  FEES REPORTED DELINQUENT
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING THE
  REVISED DELINQUENT SANITATION ACCOUNT REPORT OF JUNE 22,
  2021, ORDERING THE PLACEMENT OF LIENS UPON REAL PROPERTY
  FOR THE UNPAID SANITATION AND SEWER MAINTENANCE FEES
  REPORTED DELINQUENT.
  Attachment(s):  Resolution

18. ADOPTION OF THE VILLAGE SOUTH SPECIFIC PLAN (SPECIFIC PLAN 15, FILE
  #17-SP01), ASSOCIATED CODE AMENDMENT AND ZONE CHANGE (FILE #21-CA01),
  GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT (FILE #21-GPA02), AND CERTIFICATION OF THE
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT (STATE CLEARINGHOUSE NO. 2019080072) FOR A
  SPECIFIC PLAN TO FACILITATE MIXED-USE TRANSIT-ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT IN
  THE SPECIFIC PLAN AREA LOCATED IMMEDIATELY SOUTH OF THE VILLAGE
  EXPANSION AREA. APPLICANT - CITY OF CLAREMONT (FUNDING SOURCES: METRO
  TRANSIT-ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT PLANNING GRANT, SB2 PLANNING GRANT, AND
  GENERAL FUND)
 Page 8  City Council Agenda  June 22, 2021

  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  A. Adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, CERTIFYING THE FINAL ENVIRONMENTAL
  IMPACT REPORT (EIR) FOR THE VILLAGE SOUTH SPECIFIC PLAN AND
  RELATED IMPLEMENTING ACTIONS AS ADEQUATE AND COMPLETE,
  APPROVING CERTAIN FINDINGS RELATED THERETO, ADOPTING A
  STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS, AND ADOPTING A
  MITIGATION MONITORING PROGRAM;
  B. Adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING THE VILLAGE SOUTH SPECIFIC
  PLAN;
  C. Adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING A GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT
  (21-GPA02) TO IMPLEMENT THE VILLAGE SOUTH SPECIFIC PLAN BY
  AMENDING CHAPTER 2 OF THE GENERAL PLAN (THE LAND USE,
  COMMUNITY CHARACTER, AND HERITAGE PRESERVATION ELEMENT)
  TO ADD A NEW LAND USE DESIGNATION TITLED "INDIAN HILL/VILLAGE
  SOUTH TRANSIT-ORIENTED MIXED USE" AND BY AMENDING FIGURE
  2-3 OF CHAPTER 2 (THE LAND USE PLAN) TO CHANGE THE GENERAL
  PLAN LAND USE DESIGNATIONS FOR ALL OF THE PROPERTIES
  LOCATED WITHIN THE VILLAGE SOUTH SPECIFIC PLAN AREA TO A
  "MIXED USE" AREA TITLED "INDIAN HILL/VILLAGE SOUTH MIXED USE
  TOD"; AND
  D. Introduce AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING A CODE AMENDMENT AND ZONE
  CHANGE (21-CA01) TO IMPLEMENT THE VILLAGE SOUTH SPECIFIC
  PLAN BY AMENDING SECTION 16.081.020 OF THE CLAREMONT
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO ADD A NEW SPECIFIC PLAN AREA TITLED
  "SPECIFIC PLAN AREA NO. 15 (VILLAGE SOUTH SPECIFIC PLAN)" AND
  BY AMENDING THE CITY OF CLAREMONT'S OFFICIAL ZONING MAP TO
  CHANGE THE ZONING DESIGNATIONS OF ALL PROPERTIES LOCATED
  IN THE VILLAGE SOUTH SPECIFIC PLAN AREA TO "SPECIFIC PLAN
  AREA 15 (SP15)", for first reading and that reading be by title only.
 Page 9  City Council Agenda  June 22, 2021

  Attachment(s):  Resolution Certifying the EIR for the Village South Specific Plan
  Resolution Adopting the Village South Specific Plan
  Resolution Adopting the General Plan Amendment
  Ordinance to add Specific Plan 15 (VSSP) to Section 16.081.020 of the CMC
  Traffic Signal Warrant Study for Bucknell Avenue and Arrow Highway
  Addendum to Project Traffic Study

  Excerpt from the 2/10/21 Architectural Commission Minutes
  5/18/21 Planning Commission Minutes
  Excerpt from the 06/01/21 Planning Commission Minutes

ORDINANCES - None

ADMINISTRATIVE ITEM
19. AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  INLAND VALLEY HUMANE SOCIETY FOR ANIMAL CONTROL SERVICES (FUNDING
  SOURCE: GENERAL FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a two-year agreement with the Inland Valley Humane Society effective
  July 1, 2021, in an amount not to exceed $360,000 annually, plus a
  Consumer Price Index (CPI) adjustment (not to exceed four percent) in
  2022-23.

CONTINUED PUBLIC COMMENT
This time is reserved for those persons who were unable to speak earlier in the agenda because
of the 30-minute time restriction.

909-399-5461.

ACCOMMODATION IN ORDER TO PARTICIPATE IN A CITY MEETING SHOULD CONTACT THE
CITY CLERK AT 909-399-5461 “VOICE” OR 1-800-735-2929 “TT/TTY” AT LEAST THREE (3)
